i: Used to say "A is B". It is like "am/is/are" in English, but it comes at the end of the sentence.

tp: In English, "is" comes in the middle, as in "I am a student", but in Korean it comes at the end, as in "저는 학생이에요".
မြန်မာစကားကဲ့သို့ပင် "ဖြစ်ပါတယ်" သည် အဆုံးတွင် လာပါသည်: "ကျွန်ုပ် ကျောင်းသား ပါ" = 저는 학생이에요။
끝을 올려 말하면 질문이 됩니다. "학생이에요?"
အဆုံးတွင် အသံ တင်လျှင် မေးခွန်း ဖြစ်သွားပါသည်: "학생이에요?" (ကျောင်းသားလား)။
명사와 "이에요"는 붙여 씁니다.
နာမ်နှင့် "이에요" ကို ကြားမခြားဘဲ တွဲရေးပါ။
dl: ဂျွန်ဂျူ တက္ကသိုလ်

အမေရိကန် လူမျိုး ပါ။
sm: 받침이 있으면 "이에요", 없으면 "예요"입니다.
받침 ရှိလျှင် "이에요"၊ မရှိလျှင် "예요" ကို သုံးပါ။

i: "이에요/예요"와 뜻이 같지만 더 공식적인 말입니다. 수업 발표, 면접, 자기소개, 손님 앞에서 씁니다.
"이에요/예요" နှင့် အဓိပ္ပာယ် တူသော်လည်း ပိုတရားဝင်ပါသည်။ အလုပ်ခွင်၊ အင်တာဗျူး၊ တင်ပြချက်များနှင့် ဖောက်သည်များ ရှေ့တွင် သုံးပါ။
m: 받침과 관계없이 명사 뒤에 "입니다"를 붙입니다. 물을 때는 "입니까?"입니다.
받침 ရှိသည် ဖြစ်စေ မရှိသည် ဖြစ်စေ နာမ် အားလုံး၏ နောက်တွင် "입니다" ကို ထည့်ပါ။ မေးရန် "입니까?" ကို သုံးပါ။

နေကောင်းသည် (မင်္ဂလာပါ)

tp: "입니다"는 [임니다]로 소리 납니다.
"입니다" ကို [임니다] (imnida) ဟု အသံထွက်ပါသည်။
대답할 때 "네, 학생입니다", 아닐 때는 "아닙니다"를 씁니다.
ဟုတ်ကြောင်း ဖြေရန် "네, 학생입니다" ဟု ပြောပြီး မဟုတ်ကြောင်း ဖြေရန် "아닙니다" ကို သုံးပါ။
발표나 면접에서는 처음부터 끝까지 "-입니다, -습니다" 말투로 말합니다.
အတန်း တင်ပြချက် သို့မဟုတ် အင်တာဗျူးတွင် "-입니다, -습니다" ပုံစံကို အစမှ အဆုံးထိ သုံးပါ။

ဆမ် ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။
ဘယ်နိုင်ငံက လာသလဲ။
ကျွန်ုပ် ဂရိ လူမျိုး ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။
sm: 공식적인 자리에서는 "입니다", 물을 때는 "입니까?"를 씁니다.
တရားဝင် အခြေအနေတွင် "입니다" ကို၊ မေးရန် "입니까?" ကို သုံးပါ။

i: "~이/가 아니다" means "is not".
"~이/가 아니다" သည် "... မဟုတ်ပါ" ဟု အဓိပ္ပာယ်ရပါသည်။
m: 받침이 있는 명사 뒤에는 "이 아니에요", 받침이 없는 명사 뒤에는 "가 아니에요"를 씁니다. 공식적인 말은 "아닙니다"입니다.
받침 ရှိသော နာမ်နောက်တွင် "이 아니에요"၊ မရှိလျှင် "가 아니에요" ကို သုံးပါ။ တရားဝင် ပုံစံမှာ "아닙니다" ဖြစ်ပါသည်။

အဲဒီလူက ကျွန်ုပ့် သူငယ်ချင်း မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။

ဒီမှာ၊ ဒီနေရာ
tp: In English, "not" comes before the noun (not a student), but in Korean "아니에요" comes after the noun.
မြန်မာစကားကဲ့သို့ပင် "아니에요" သည် နာမ်၏ နောက်တွင် လာပါသည်: "ကျောင်းသား မဟုတ်ပါ" = 학생이 아니에요။
"아니요" is the answer "no", and "아니에요" is the sentence ending "is not". "아니요, 학생이 아니에요."
"아니요" သည် အဖြေ (မဟုတ်ပါ) ဖြစ်ပြီး "아니에요" သည် ဝါကျအဆုံးသတ် (... မဟုတ်ပါ) ဖြစ်ပါသည်: "아니요, 학생이 아니에요."
말할 때는 "이/가"를 자주 뺍니다. "학생 아니에요."
စကားပြောရာတွင် "이/가" ကို မကြာခဏ ချန်ထားကြပါသည်: "학생 아니에요."
dl: ဆမ်၊ ဒါ ဆမ့် အိတ်လား။
မဟုတ်ပါဘူး၊ ကျွန်ုပ့် အိတ် မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။
ဒါဆို ဘယ်သူ့ ဟာလဲ။
sm: "Noun + 이/가 아니에요" means "is not + noun".
"နာမ် + 이/가 아니에요" သည် "... မဟုတ်ပါ" ဟု အဓိပ္ပာယ်ရပါသည်။
qz: "ကျောင်းသား မဟုတ်ပါ"을 한국어로?

i: "있어요" means "have" or "be (somewhere)", and "없어요" means "don't have" or "not be (there)".
"있어요" သည် "ရှိသည်" (ပိုင်ဆိုင်ခြင်း သို့မဟုတ် တစ်နေရာရာတွင် ရှိခြင်း)၊ "없어요" သည် "မရှိပါ" ဟု အဓိပ္ပာယ်ရပါသည်။
m: 가진 것은 "명사 + 이/가 있어요", 있는 곳은 "곳 + 에 있어요"로 말합니다.
ပိုင်ဆိုင်သော အရာအတွက် "နာမ် + 이/가 있어요" ဟု ပြောပါ။ တည်ရှိရာ နေရာအတွက် "နေရာ + 에 있어요" ဟု ပြောပါ။

အိမ်မှာ ရှိတယ်

မေးခွန်း ရှိပါတယ်

အခု အချိန် မရှိဘူး။

tp: In English, "have" and "be (somewhere)" are different words, but in Korean both are "있다". If there is "에", it means "be (somewhere)".
မြန်မာစကားကဲ့သို့ပင် ကိုရီးယားတွင် ပိုင်ဆိုင်ခြင်းနှင့် တည်ရှိခြင်း နှစ်ခုစလုံးအတွက် "있다" (ရှိသည်) ကို သုံးပါသည်။ "에" ပါလျှင် "...မှာ ရှိသည်" ဟု အဓိပ္ပာယ်ရပါသည်။
"없어요"는 "안 있어요"라고 하지 않습니다.
"없어요" အစား "안 있어요" ဟု မပြောပါနှင့်။
높이는 사람이 있는 곳은 "계세요"를 씁니다. "교수님은 연구실에 계세요."
လေးစားရသူ ရှိရာ နေရာအတွက် "계세요" ကို သုံးပါ: "교수님은 연구실에 계세요." (ပါမောက္ခက ရုံးခန်းမှာ ရှိပါတယ်။)
dl: ဆမ်၊ မနက်ဖြန် အချိန် ရှိလား။
မနက်ပိုင်း မရှိဘူး။ နေ့လယ်ပိုင်း အချိန် ရှိတယ်။
မနက်ပိုင်း (နေ့လယ် မတိုင်မီ)
နေ့လယ်ပိုင်း (နေ့လယ် နောက်)
그럼 오후에 만나요. 어디에 있을 거예요?
ဒါဆို နေ့လယ်ပိုင်း တွေ့ကြရအောင်။ ဘယ်မှာ ရှိမလဲ။
နေ့လယ်ပိုင်း (နေ့လယ် နောက်)
geureom ohu-e mannayo eodie isseul kkeoyeyo?
အဆောင်မှာ ရှိမယ်။
sm: "있다" means "have" and "be (there)"; "없다" means "don't have" and "not be (there)".
"있다" သည် "ရှိသည်"၊ "없다" သည် "မရှိ" ဟု အဓိပ္ပာယ်ရပါသည်။
qz: "ပိုက်ဆံ မရှိဘူး"을 한국어로?

i: 한국어 문장은 "누가 + 무엇을 + 하다" 순서입니다. 동사가 맨 끝에 옵니다. 영어와 가장 크게 다른 점입니다.
ကိုရီးယား ဝါကျသည် "ဘယ်သူ + ဘာကို + လုပ်သည်" ဖြစ်ပါသည်။ ကြိယာသည် အဆုံးဆုံးတွင် လာပါသည်။ ဤအစီအစဉ်သည် မြန်မာစကားနှင့် အတူတူ ဖြစ်ပါသည်။
m: English: I(저) eat(먹다) rice(밥). Korean: 저는 밥을 먹어요. Small words (particles) like "은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에" are added after nouns to show their role in the sentence.

မြန်မာ: ကျွန်ုပ် ထမင်း စားတယ်။ ကိုရီးယား: 저는 밥을 먹어요 (ကျွန်ုပ် ထမင်း စား)။ မြန်မာ "က၊ ကို၊ မှာ" ကဲ့သို့ နာမ်နောက်တွင် "은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에" ကဲ့သို့ ပစ္စည်းများ ထည့်၍ ဝါကျတွင် ၎င်းတို့၏ အခန်းကဏ္ဍကို ပြပါသည်။
e: ကျွန်ုပ် ထမင်း စားတယ်။
ထမင်း၊ အစာ
ဆမ်က ကျောင်း သွားတယ်။
ကျွန်ုပ် ကိုရီးယားစာ သင်တယ်။
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
ကျွန်ုပ် မနေ့က ဈေးမှာ သစ်သီး ဝယ်ခဲ့တယ်။
အိတ်ကြီး တစ်လုံး ရှိတယ်။
tp: A describing word comes before the word it describes. "A big bag" in English is "큰 가방" in Korean.
ဖော်ပြသော စကားလုံးသည် ၎င်း ဖော်ပြသည့် စကားလုံး၏ ရှေ့တွင် လာပါသည်: "큰 가방" (ကြီးသော အိတ်)။ မြန်မာ "အိတ်ကြီး" နှင့် အစီအစဉ် ပြောင်းပြန် ဖြစ်ပါသည်။
"Whose what" also comes in the owner-first order. "My house" is "제 집".
"ဘယ်သူ့" သည်လည်း ရှေ့တွင် လာပါသည်: "ကျွန်ုပ့် အိမ်" သည် "제 집" ဖြစ်ပါသည်။
dl: ဆမ်၊ အခု ဘာ လုပ်နေလဲ။
ကိုရီးယားစာ သင်နေတယ်။
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
ဘယ်မှာ စာကျက်လဲ။
ဘယ်မှာ (လုပ်ဆောင်ရာ နေရာ)
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
အဆောင်မှာ စာကျက်တယ်။
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
sm: 한국어는 동사가 문장 끝에 오고, 꾸미는 말이 앞에 옵니다.
qz: 순서에 맞는 것은? 저는 먹어요 밥을 / 저는 밥을 먹어요

i: In Korean, a sentence becomes a question when you raise your voice at the end. You do not need to change the word order like in English ("Do you…?", "Are you…?").
ကိုရီးယားတွင် အဆုံး၌ အသံ တင်လျှင် မေးခွန်း ဖြစ်ပါသည်။ မြန်မာကဲ့သို့ "လား" ထည့်ရန် သို့မဟုတ် အစီအစဉ် ပြောင်းရန် မလိုပါ။

ကျန်းမာသည်
tp: In English you show respect with words like "sir" or "please", but in Korean you show respect by putting "-시-" inside the verb.
In English you show respect with words like "sir" or "please", but in Korean you put "-시-" inside the verb.
높이는 것은 "하는 사람"입니다. 듣는 사람이 친구여도 교수님 이야기를 할 때는 "교수님이 오셨어"라고 합니다.
The respect is for the person who does the action. Even if you are talking to a friend, when you talk about the professor you say "교수님이 오셨어".
dl: ရှိသည် (ယဉ်ကျေး)
지금 수업 중이십니다. 삼십 분 후에 끝나십니다.
She is in class now. It will finish in 30 minutes.
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
jigeum su-eop jungisimnida samsip bun hu-e kkeunnasimnida
sm: 높이는 사람이 하는 일에는 동사에 "-(으)시-"를 넣습니다.
For the actions of a respected person, put "-(으)시-" in the verb.
qz: 맞는 것은? 제가 가시겠습니다 / 제가 가겠습니다

i: "이/가"의 높임말입니다. 높이는 사람이 주어일 때 씁니다.
This is the respectful form of "이/가". Use it when a respected person is the subject.
m: 사람 뒤에 붙이고, 동사에는 "-(으)시-"를 함께 씁니다. "은/는"의 높임은 "께서는", "도"의 높임은 "께서도"입니다.
Add it after a person and also use "-(으)시-" in the verb. The respectful form of "은/는" is "께서는", and of "도" is "께서도".
c: the head of the department (respectful, subject)
교수님 ပါမောက္ခ
e: ချက်ပြုတ်သည်
The head of the department said so.
tp: "께서"는 격식 있는 말과 글에서 씁니다. 일상 대화에서는 "어머니가 요리하세요"처럼 "이/가"에 "-시-"만 써도 됩니다.
"께서" is used in formal speech and writing. In everyday talk, you can just use "이/가" with "-시-", as in "어머니가 요리하세요".
높임말 낱말과 함께 씁니다. 말 → 말씀, 집 → 댁, 나이 → 연세, 이름 → 성함, 밥 → 진지, 아프다 → 편찮으시다.
It is used with respectful words: 말 → 말씀, 집 → 댁, 나이 → 연세, 이름 → 성함, 밥 → 진지, 아프다 → 편찮으시다.
dl: The head of the department prepared them himself.
Really? Please tell him thank you.
ကျေးဇူးတင်သည်
ပေးသည် (주세요 = ... ပေးပါ)
sm: 높이는 사람이 주어이면 "께서"와 "-(으)시-"를 함께 씁니다.
When a respected person is the subject, use "께서" together with "-(으)시-".

i: 친한 친구, 나이가 어린 사람, 가족에게 쓰는 편한 말입니다. 학교에서는 선배가 후배에게 쓰기도 합니다.
This is casual speech used with close friends, younger people and family. At work, older or senior people may also use it with junior people.
m: "-아요/어요"에서 "요"를 뺍니다. "이에요/예요"는 "이야/야"가 됩니다. "네"는 "응", "아니요"는 "아니"입니다.
Take "요" off "-아요/어요". "이에요/예요" becomes "이야/야". "네" becomes "응", and "아니요" becomes "아니".
c: 뭐 해요? ဘာ လုပ်နေလဲ။
ဘာ လုပ်နေလဲ။
e: ထမင်း၊ အစာ
အတူ သွားကြရအောင်။
tp: 반말은 알아듣는 것이 먼저입니다. 내가 쓸 때는 상대가 "말 편하게 해요", "말 놓으세요"라고 한 뒤에 씁니다.
First, learn to understand casual speech. Use it yourself only after the other person says "말 편하게 해요" or "말 놓으세요" (You can speak casually).
선배나 나이 많은 친구가 반말을 해도 나는 "-요"로 대답합니다. 무시하는 뜻이 아닐 때가 많습니다.
Even if an older student (선배) or an older friend speaks casually to you, answer with "-요". Often they do not mean to be rude.
dl: ထမင်း၊ အစာ
sm: 반말은 "-아요/어요"에서 "요"를 뺀 말이고, 친한 사이에만 씁니다.
Casual speech is "-아요/어요" without "요", and you use it only with people you are close to.
qz: 선배가 반말로 물었습니다. 나는 어떻게 대답합니까? 응, 했어 / 네, 했어요

i: Some verbs don't add "-(으)시-" to show respect; they use a completely different word. It is a bit like English using "dine" instead of "eat".
Some verbs don't add "-(으)시-" to show respect; they use a completely different word. It is a bit like English using "dine" instead of "eat".
w: Please eat a lot. (Enjoy your meal.)
မသည်၊ သယ်သည်
Professor, would you like some coffee?
My grandmother goes to bed early.
Did you sleep well last night?
The department head is in the department office now.
When the professor is speaking, take notes.
နေမကောင်းသည် (ရိုသေစကား)
ဘယ်နေရာ နာလဲ။
ဘယ်နေရာ (ကတ္တား)
임현정 교수님이 편찮으셔서 오늘 수업이 없어요.
imhyeonjeong gyosunimi pyeonchaneusyeoseo oneul su-eobi eopseoyo
Professor Im Hyeonjeong is sick, so there is no class today.
နေမကောင်းသည် (ရိုသေစကား)
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
tp: 자기에게는 쓰지 않습니다. "많이 드세요"에 "네, 많이 먹겠습니다"라고 대답합니다. "드시겠습니다"는 틀립니다.
Don't use these for yourself. To "많이 드세요", answer "네, 많이 먹겠습니다". "드시겠습니다" is wrong.
"안녕히 가세요"는 떠나는 사람에게, "안녕히 계세요"는 남는 사람에게 하는 인사입니다.
"안녕히 가세요" is said to the person leaving, and "안녕히 계세요" to the person staying.
"있다" has two honorific forms. When a person "is (somewhere)", use "계시다"; when someone "has" something, use "있으시다". "시간 있으세요?"
"있다" has two honorific forms. When a person "is (somewhere)", use "계시다"; when someone "has" something, use "있으시다": "시간 있으세요?"
dl: Did you have lunch? (to the TA)
သင်ကြားရေး လက်ထောက်
Not yet. How about you, Sam?
저도 아직 안 먹었습니다. 교수님은 연구실에 계세요?
I haven't eaten yet either. Is the professor in her office?
jeodo ajik an meogeotseumnida gyosunimeun yeon-gusire geseyo?
No, she is sick today, so she didn't come in.
နေမကောင်းသည် (ရိုသေစကား)
sm: 먹다 → 드시다, 자다 → 주무시다, 있다 → 계시다, 말하다 → 말씀하시다, 아프다 → 편찮으시다.
먹다 → 드시다, 자다 → 주무시다, 있다 → 계시다, 말하다 → 말씀하시다, 아프다 → 편찮으시다.
qz: "많이 드세요"에 맞는 대답은? 많이 드시겠습니다 / 많이 먹겠습니다

i: 내가 윗사람에게 하는 동작을 낮추어 말해서 상대를 높이는 낱말입니다. 높이는 사람은 동작을 받는 사람입니다.
These words make your own action toward an older or higher person humble, to show respect. The person you respect is the one who receives the action.
w: to give (to an older or higher person)
I gave the assignment to the professor.
အိမ်စာ၊ တာဝန်
On the holiday, I gave the professor some Greek coffee.
သင်ကြားရေး လက်ထောက်
I'll ask the professor about the exam date.
မနက်ဖြန် တွေ့မယ်။
I'll see you at the interview tomorrow.
to take, to escort (an older or higher person)
I took the guest to the hotel.
ဧည့်သည်၊ ဖောက်သည်
အထိ၊ မတိုင်ခင်
I live with my parents and take care of them.
နေထိုင်သည်
Please take the guest to the department office.
ဧည့်သည်၊ ဖောက်သည်
I have something to tell you.
to give (humble) (드릴 말씀 = something to tell you)
I told the professor that I would be absent because I'm sick.
နာသည်၊ ဖျားသည်
tp: 두 가지 높임을 가려 씁니다. 윗사람이 하는 일은 "-(으)시-"(교수님이 주셨어요), 내가 윗사람에게 하는 일은 낮추는 말(교수님께 드렸어요)입니다.
Use the two kinds of respect correctly. For what an older person does, use "-(으)시-" (교수님이 주셨어요); for what you do for an older person, use the humble word (교수님께 드렸어요).
"-아/어 주다"도 "-아/어 드리다"가 됩니다. 식당과 가게에서 "해 드릴게요", "가져다드리겠습니다"를 많이 씁니다.
"-아/어 주다" also becomes "-아/어 드리다". In restaurants and shops you often hear "해 드릴게요" and "가져다드리겠습니다".
dl: Professor, I have something to tell you.
to give (humble) (드릴 말씀 = something to tell you)
May I ask you something about the scholarship?
Of course. Give the application form to me.
Okay, I'll give it to you tomorrow.
ပေးသည် (ယဉ်ကျေးစကား)
sm: 내가 윗사람에게 하는 일은 "드리다, 여쭙다, 뵙다, 모시다, 말씀드리다"로 말합니다.
For your actions toward older or higher people, use "드리다, 여쭙다, 뵙다, 모시다, 말씀드리다".

i: 윗사람과 관계있는 것을 말할 때 쓰는 높임 명사입니다.
These are honorific nouns used when talking about things related to older or higher people.
w: ဒီမှာ နာမည် ရေးပါ။
May I know the name of the person in charge?
May I ask how old you are?
I went to the professor's house.
I was invited to the professor's house.
ဖိတ်ခံရသည်
ထမင်းစားခြင်း
Excuse me, may I ask something?
I've heard a lot about you.
ကြားသည်၊ နားထောင်သည်
ဟိုလူက ဘယ်သူလဲ။
That is the new head of the department.
tp: 높임 명사를 쓰면 동사도 높입니다. "이름이 뭐예요?"(보통) "성함이 어떻게 되세요?"(높임).
If you use an honorific noun, use an honorific verb too. "이름이 뭐예요?" (normal), "성함이 어떻게 되세요?" (honorific).
"진지"는 집안 어른께 쓰는 말이고, 학교와 가게에서는 "식사"를 씁니다. "식사하셨어요?"는 한국의 인사말입니다.
"진지" is used for elders in the family; at school and in shops use "식사". "식사하셨어요?" (Have you eaten?) is a Korean greeting.
dl: Welcome. May I have your name?
လာသည် (မိုးရွာသည်)
I'm Park Minha. I came to see Professor Sim Yeongguk.
네, 교수님께 말씀드리겠습니다. 이쪽에서 잠시만 기다려 주십시오.
Yes, I'll let the professor know. Please wait here for a moment.
ပေးသည် (ရိုသေစကား)
ne, gyosunimkke malsseumdeurigetseumnida ijjogeseo jamsiman gidaryeo jusipsio
sm: 이름 → 성함, 나이 → 연세, 집 → 댁, 밥 → 식사, 말 → 말씀, 사람 → 분.
이름 → 성함, 나이 → 연세, 집 → 댁, 밥 → 식사, 말 → 말씀, 사람 → 분.
qz: 맞는 것은? 제 성함은 샘입니다 / 제 이름은 샘입니다

i: Korean shows respect to the listener by using a humble word for "I". English has no humble "I", so practice "저" carefully.
Korean shows respect to the listener by using a humble word for "I". English has no humble form of "I", so practice "저" carefully.
w: ကျွန်ုပ် ဆမ် ပါ။
ဥဇဘက်ကစ္စတန်
လာသည် (မိုးရွာသည်)
to do wrong, to make a mistake
သန့်ရှင်းရေး
ကျွန်ုပ်နာမည် ဆမ် ပါ။
I'll give you my phone number.
ပေးသည် (ယဉ်ကျေးစကား)
ပြင်ဆင်သည်
ပင်ပန်းသည်
tp: "-요"나 "-습니다"로 말할 때는 "저"를 씁니다. "나는 샘입니다"는 어색합니다.
When you speak with "-요" or "-습니다", use "저". "나는 샘입니다" sounds strange.
"저가"가 아니라 "제가", "나가"가 아니라 "내가"입니다.
It is "제가", not "저가", and "내가", not "나가".
손님에게 학교나 가게를 말할 때 "저희 학교, 저희 가게"라고 합니다. 그러나 나라는 낮추지 않고 "우리나라"라고 합니다.
When you talk about your school or shop to guests, say "저희 학교, 저희 가게". But you don't lower your country; say "우리나라".
dl: 누가 이 발표를 할 수 있어요?
nuga i balpyoreul hal su isseoyo?
တစ်ယောက်တည်း
Our team can do it together.
sm: 윗사람 앞에서는 "나, 내가, 내, 우리" 대신 "저, 제가, 제, 저희"를 씁니다.
In front of older or higher people, use "저, 제가, 제, 저희" instead of "나, 내가, 내, 우리".
qz: 맞는 것은? 저가 하겠습니다 / 제가 하겠습니다
"ကျွန်ုပ်၏"을 낮추어 말하면?

i: 한국어는 같은 인사도 상대에 따라 세 가지 말씨로 합니다. 격식(-습니다), 부드러운 높임(-요), 반말입니다.
In Korean, the same greeting has three speech styles depending on the listener: formal (-습니다), soft polite (-요) and casual (반말).
w: မင်္ဂလာပါ။ ကျွန်ုပ် ဆမ် ပါ။
안녕하십니까? 오늘부터 이 수업을 듣게 된 샘입니다.
annyeonghasimnikka? oneulbuteo i su-eobeul deutke doen saemimnida
Hello. I'm Sam, and I'm taking this class from today.
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
(တွေ့ရ၍) ဝမ်းသာသည်
Hello. Nice to meet you. (first meeting)
안녕하세요? 이 층에 새로 이사 왔어요.
annyeonghaseyo? i cheunge saero isa wasseoyo
Hello. I just moved to this floor.
လာသည် (မိုးရွာသည်)
စနေ တနင်္ဂနွေ
Thank you so much for interpreting.
ပေးသည် (ရိုသေစကား)
တကယ် ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်။
Thank you for lending me the umbrella.
နောက်ကျလို့ တောင်းပန်ပါတယ်။
နောက်ကျသည်
I'm sorry. I won't be late again.
ထပ်မံ၊ ပြန်
နောက်ကျသည်
Sorry. I couldn't answer the phone.
လက်ခံရရှိသည်
tp: English "hello" is the same for everyone, but in Korean the form changes with the listener. If you don't know which to use, use "-요".
English "hello" is the same for everyone, but in Korean the form changes with the listener. If you are not sure which to use, use "-요".
윗사람에게 "미안해요, 고마워요"는 가볍게 들립니다. "죄송합니다, 감사합니다"를 씁니다.
To older or higher people, "미안해요, 고마워요" sounds too light. Use "죄송합니다, 감사합니다".
"안녕"은 만날 때와 헤어질 때 다 쓰지만 친구나 동생에게만 씁니다.
"안녕" is used both when meeting and when leaving, but only with friends and younger people.
dl: နေကောင်းသည် (안녕하세요 = မင်္ဂလာပါ)
아, 샘 씨. 안녕하세요? 수업은 들을 만해요?
Oh, Sam. Hello. Is the class okay for you?
နေကောင်းသည် (안녕하세요 = မင်္ဂလာပါ)
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
to be okay to do, worth doing
a, saem ssi annyeonghaseyo? su-eobeun deureul manhaeyo?
ဟုတ်ကဲ့၊ ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်။
ကျေးဇူးတင်သည်
Sam, hi! Did you have lunch?
sm: 인사는 격식 "-습니다", 부드러운 "-요", 반말 세 단계가 있습니다.
Greetings have three levels: formal "-습니다", soft "-요", and casual.

i: 묻는 말도 세 가지 말씨가 있습니다. 듣는 사람이 윗사람이면 "-(으)시-"도 넣습니다.
Questions also have three speech styles. If the listener is older or higher, also add "-(으)시-".
w: Where are you going? I'll take you there.
교수님, 어디 가십니까? 제가 가방을 들어 드릴까요?
gyosunim, eodi gasimnikka? jega gabangeul deureo deurilkkayo?
Professor, where are you going? Shall I carry your bag?
to give (polite) (-아/어 드리다 = do for someone)
ဘယ် သွားမလို့လဲ။
Where are you going? (to a senior)
Where are you going at this hour?
အချိန်၊ နာရီ
It's your day off. Where are you going?
Where are you going? Let's go together.
အတန်းပြီးရင် ဘယ် သွားမလဲ။
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
နေကောင်းသည် (안녕하세요 = မင်္ဂလာပါ)
Have you eaten? Would you like to go together? (to the TA)
သင်ကြားရေး လက်ထောက်
Did you eat? Want to eat together?
Did you eat? Shall I make ramyeon?
ရာမျွန် (အသင့်စား ခေါက်ဆွဲ)
ပြုတ်သည်၊ ချက်သည်
Are you sick? Are you okay?
နာသည်၊ ဖျားသည်
Did you fall? Are you okay?
You don't look well. Are you okay?
ပုံပေါ်သည် (-아/어 보이다)
tp: 윗사람이 하는 일을 물을 때는 말끝만 바꾸지 않고 "-(으)시-"를 넣습니다. "어디 가요?"가 아니라 "어디 가세요?"입니다.
When you ask about what an older or higher person does, don't just change the ending; add "-(으)시-". Say "어디 가세요?", not "어디 가요?".
"어디 가세요?", "식사하셨어요?"는 인사입니다. 자세히 대답하지 않아도 됩니다. "네, 잠깐 나가요", "네, 먹었습니다".
"어디 가세요?" and "식사하셨어요?" are greetings. You don't need to answer in detail: "네, 잠깐 나가요", "네, 먹었습니다".

sm: 윗사람에게 물을 때는 "-(으)세요?"나 "-(으)십니까?"를 씁니다.
When you ask older or higher people, use "-(으)세요?" or "-(으)십니까?".

Requests and instructions also have three speech styles. The more polite a request is, the longer it gets.

tp: 윗사람에게 부탁할 때는 시키는 모양보다 묻는 모양이 더 공손합니다. "-아/어 주시겠어요?", "-아/어 주실 수 있으세요?"
When you ask an older or higher person, a question form is more polite than an order form: "-아/어 주시겠어요?", "-아/어 주실 수 있으세요?"
부탁 앞에 "죄송하지만", "실례지만", "바쁘시겠지만"을 붙이면 더 부드럽습니다.
Adding "죄송하지만", "실례지만" or "바쁘시겠지만" (I know you're busy, but…) before a request makes it softer.

i: 대답하는 말도 말씨에 따라 달라집니다. 수업과 아르바이트에서는 대답을 또렷하게 하는 것이 중요합니다.
Answers also change with the speech style. In class and at a part-time job, it is important to answer clearly.
w: Understood. I'll do it right away.
အထိ၊ မတိုင်ခင်

tp: 윗사람에게 "응", "어"라고 대답하면 큰 실례입니다. 꼭 "네"나 "예"라고 합니다.
Answering an older or higher person with "응" or "어" is very rude. Always say "네" or "예".
못 알아들었는데 "네"라고 하지 않습니다. "죄송합니다. 잘 못 들었습니다", "다시 한번 말씀해 주십시오"라고 합니다. 모르면서 "네"라고 하면 나중에 문제가 생깁니다.
Don't say "네" if you didn't understand. Say "죄송합니다. 잘 못 들었습니다" or "다시 한번 말씀해 주십시오". Saying "네" when you don't understand causes problems later.
"네" means not only "yes" but also "I'm listening". It is also the answer when someone calls you: "샘 씨!" "네!"
"네" means not only "yes" but is also used to show "I'm listening". It is also the answer when someone calls your name: "샘 씨!" "네!"

To older or higher people answer "네, 알겠습니다"; if you didn't understand, say "잘 못 들었습니다".

i: 같은 뜻의 말을 듣는 사람에 따라 바꾸는 연습입니다. 말씨는 나이, 관계, 친한 정도로 정합니다.
This is practice changing words with the same meaning for different listeners. The speech style depends on age, your relationship and how close you are.

Thank you for your hard work today too.

Thank you for your hard work today. (to the TA)

good work (said to someone younger or lower)

Thank you for your hard work. I'll be going now.

tp: 처음 만난 사람에게는 나이와 관계없이 "-요"를 씁니다. 반말은 상대가 "말 편하게 해요"라고 한 뒤에 씁니다.
With people you meet for the first time, use "-요" whatever their age. Use casual speech only after the other person says "말 편하게 해요".
한국 대학에서는 나이보다 먼저 입학한 순서(학번)가 앞서기도 합니다. 나이가 어려도 선배에게는 높임말을 씁니다.
At Korean universities, who entered first (학번, entry year) often matters more than age. Even if they are younger, use polite speech with seniors.

sm: 교수님과 손님에게는 격식, 선배와 처음 만난 친구에게는 "-요", 친한 친구에게만 반말을 씁니다.
Use the formal style with professors and guests, "-요" with seniors and new classmates, and casual speech only with close friends.

i: Used to talk about past events. English uses a past form of the verb (worked, went), and Korean also changes the verb by adding "-았/었-".
Used to talk about the past. English uses a past form of the verb (worked, went); Korean puts "-았/었-" in the verb.
m: "-아요/어요"와 같은 규칙입니다. ㅏ, ㅗ 뒤에는 "-았어요", 그 밖에는 "-었어요", 하다는 "했어요"입니다. 명사는 "이었어요/였어요"입니다.
It follows the same rule as "-아요/어요". After ㅏ, ㅗ use "-았어요"; otherwise use "-었어요"; 하다 becomes "했어요". For nouns use "이었어요/였어요".

Even with words like "어제", you must change the verb. "어제 가요" is wrong; "어제 갔어요" is right. (Just like "Yesterday I go" is wrong in English.)
격식 있는 말은 "-았습니다/었습니다"입니다. 했습니다, 갔습니다.
The formal form is "-았습니다/었습니다": 했습니다, 갔습니다.
"아직 안 했어요" means "I haven't done it yet", and "벌써 했어요" means "I already did it".
"아직 안 했어요" means "I haven't done it yet", and "벌써 했어요" means "I already did it".

i: Used to talk about things you will do or plans. It is like "will, be going to" in English. It also shows a guess (probably will).
Used to talk about things you will do or plans. It is like "will, be going to" in English. It is also used for guesses (probably will).
m: 받침이 있으면 "-을 거예요", 받침이 없으면 "-ㄹ 거예요"를 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 그대로 "거예요"만 붙입니다.
With a final consonant add "-을 거예요"; without one add "-ㄹ 거예요". With a ㄹ final consonant, just add "거예요".

tp: In English, "will" comes before the verb, but in Korean it is added after the verb. "will go" = "갈 거예요".
In English, "will" comes before the verb, but in Korean it is added after it: "will go" = "갈 거예요".
"거예요"는 [꺼예요]로 소리 납니다. 갈 거예요 [갈 꺼예요].
"거예요" is pronounced [꺼예요]: 갈 거예요 [갈 꺼예요] (gal kkeoyeyo).

i: Talks about what you are doing right now. It is like "be + -ing" in English.
Tells what you are doing right now. It is like "be + -ing" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-고 있어요"를 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다. 높임은 "-고 계세요"입니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-고 있어요". The final consonant does not matter. The respectful form is "-고 계세요".

tp: 한국어는 "-아요/어요"만으로도 지금 하는 일을 말할 수 있습니다. "뭐 해요?"와 "뭐 하고 있어요?"는 거의 같습니다.
In Korean, "-아요/어요" alone can also show what you are doing now. "뭐 해요?" and "뭐 하고 있어요?" are almost the same.
입는 동사는 입은 상태도 나타냅니다. "모자를 쓰고 있어요"는 지금 쓰는 중이거나 이미 쓴 상태입니다.
Verbs for wearing also show the state of wearing something. "모자를 쓰고 있어요" means you are putting on a hat, or you are already wearing one.

i: It has two meanings. ① The speaker's strong intention (will) ② A guess (must be, it seems). It is also used in many set greetings.
It has two meanings: ① the speaker's intention (will) ② a guess (must be, it seems). It is also found in many set greetings.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-겠-"을 넣은 뒤 말끝을 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다.
Take "-다" off a verb or adjective, put in "-겠-", then add the ending. The final consonant does not matter.

tp: "알겠습니다"는 지시를 받았을 때 가장 많이 쓰는 대답입니다. "알아요"는 "이미 알고 있다"는 뜻이어서 지시에 대한 대답으로는 버릇없게 들립니다.
"알겠습니다" is the most common answer when you get an instruction. "알아요" means "I already know", so it sounds rude as an answer to an instruction.
굳어진 인사말: 처음 뵙겠습니다, 잘 먹겠습니다, 다녀오겠습니다, 실례하겠습니다.
Set greetings: 처음 뵙겠습니다 (Nice to meet you), 잘 먹겠습니다 (Thank you for the food), 다녀오겠습니다 (I'll be back), 실례하겠습니다 (Excuse me).

"제가 ~(으)ㄹ까요?" asks if there is something for you to do. At a part-time job or in a group project, people often ask "뭘 할까요?" (What shall I do?).

Don't use it with senior people. To a professor, say "가시지요" or "같이 가시겠어요?".

Professors and club leaders (선배) often use it when speaking to a group: "자, 시작합시다" (OK, let's start), "조용히 합시다" (Let's be quiet).

i: It means you have decided or agreed to do something. It is like "decide to, agree to" in English.
It means you have agreed or promised to do something. It is like "decide to, agree to" in English.

Because it has already been decided, it is usually used in the past form, like "-기로 했어요".
"-(으)려고 해요"는 내 마음속 생각이고, "-기로 했어요"는 이미 정했거나 다른 사람과 약속한 일입니다.

For a stronger suggestion, say "-는 게 좋겠어요": "병원에 가는 게 좋겠어요." (You'd better go to the hospital.)

tp: In English, "don't" comes before the verb, but in Korean "-지 마세요" comes after the verb.
In English, "don't" comes before the verb, but in Korean "-지 마세요" comes after the verb.

m: 받침이 있으면 "-으니까", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-니까"를 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(멀다 → 머니까). 지난 일은 "-았/었으니까"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-으니까"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-니까". A ㄹ 받침 drops (멀다 → 머니까). For the past, use "-았/었으니까".
c: 위험하다 အန္တရာယ်ရှိသည်
e: We don't have time, so let's go quickly.
It's hot, so don't touch it.
ပူသည် (ထိလျှင်)
ကိုင်သည်၊ ထိသည်
It's raining, so take an umbrella with you.
tp: 안전을 알리는 말은 거의 "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요" 모양입니다.
Safety warnings are almost always in the form "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요".
윗사람에게 내 사정을 말할 때 "-(으)니까"를 쓰면 따지는 것처럼 들릴 수 있습니다. "아프니까 못 가요"보다 "아파서 못 가요"가 부드럽습니다.
When you give your own reason to a senior, "-(으)니까" can sound like you are arguing. "아파서 못 가요" is softer than "아프니까 못 가요".
dl: 이 냄비는 뜨거우니까 꼭 장갑을 끼세요.
This pot is hot, so be sure to wear gloves.
to put on, wear (gloves, a ring)
i naembineun tteugeo-unikka kkok janggabeul kkiseyo
Yes, I understand. Should I wear an apron too?
ဝတ်သည် (အဝတ်)
Yes, oil splashes, so wear an apron too.
ဝတ်သည် (အဝတ်)
sm: 시키는 말 앞에서 까닭을 말할 때는 "-(으)니까"를 씁니다.
When you give a reason before an order, use "-(으)니까".
qz: 맞는 것은? 추워서 문을 닫으세요 / 추우니까 문을 닫으세요

i: Used to state a reason clearly. Often used in writing, reports and presentations. It is like "because, due to" in English.
Used to state a reason clearly. Often used in writing, reports and presentations. It is like "because, due to" in English.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-기 때문에"를 붙입니다. 지난 일은 "-았/었기 때문에", 명사는 "명사 + 때문에"입니다.
Take "-다" off and add "-기 때문에". For the past, use "-았/었기 때문에"; for nouns, use "noun + 때문에".
c: 오다 to come, (rain) ပြုတ်ကျသည်
과제 အိမ်စာ၊ တာဝန်
အိမ်စာ၊ တာဝန်
e: Because it is raining, the festival was canceled.
Because I have a lot of assignments, I'm going to the library.
အိမ်စာ၊ တာဝန်
စာကြည့်တိုက်
I went to the hospital because of a cold.
အအေးမိခြင်း
버스가 고장 났기 때문에 수업에 늦었습니다.
beoseuga gojang natki ttaemune su-eobe neujeotseumnida
Because the bus broke down, I was late for class.
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
နောက်ကျသည်
tp: 뒤에 시키는 말이나 같이 하자는 말이 올 수 없습니다.
The second part cannot be an order or a suggestion.
"명사 + 때문에"는 흔히 좋지 않은 일의 까닭입니다. 좋은 일의 까닭은 "덕분에"입니다.
"Noun + 때문에" is usually the cause of something bad. For the cause of something good, use "덕분에".
까닭을 물을 때 "왜요?", "무엇 때문에요?"라고 하고, 대답은 "~기 때문입니다"로 끝낼 수 있습니다.
To ask for a reason, say "왜요?" or "무엇 때문에요?", and you can end the answer with "~기 때문입니다".
dl: 샘 씨, 과제를 왜 늦게 냈습니까?
Sam, why did you hand in the assignment late?
အိမ်စာ၊ တာဝန်
saem ssi, gwajereul wae neutke naetseumnikka?
It's because my laptop broke down yesterday.
to be fine, to be OK
Yes, I had it repaired, so there is no problem.
sm: "-기 때문에"는 까닭을 뚜렷하게 밝히는 격식 있는 말입니다.
"-기 때문에" is a formal way to state a reason clearly.
qz: 좋은 일의 까닭에 쓰는 말은? 때문에 / 덕분에

i: Gives a condition. It is like "if" in English.
Gives a condition. It is like "if" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으면", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-면"을 붙입니다. 명사는 "(이)면"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-으면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면". For nouns, use "(이)면".
c: နာသည်၊ ဖျားသည်
내일 မနက်ဖြန်
e: If you have time, let's go together.
If it hurts, don't put up with it. Tell us.
နာသည်၊ ဖျားသည်
to put up with, hold back
I'll call you when class is over.
အတန်း၊ စာသင်ချိန်
ဖုန်းဆက်သည်
tp: English "if" comes at the start of the condition, but "-(으)면" is added to its end: "if you don't know" = "모르면".
English "if" comes at the start of the condition, but "-(으)면" is added to its end: "if you don't know" = "모르면".
It is also used for things that will surely happen. Then it means "when": "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (When spring comes, it gets warm.)
It is also used for things that will surely happen. Then it means "when": "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (When spring comes, it gets warm.)
앞에 "만약, 만일, 혹시"를 넣어서 조건임을 뚜렷하게 할 수 있습니다. "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요."
You can add "만약, 만일, 혹시" in front to make the condition clear: "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요." (If you are late, please contact me.)
dl: What do you do if there is a fire in the dorm?
to break out (불이 나다 = a fire breaks out)
I go outside right away and call 119.
ထွက်သွားသည်
ဖုန်းဆက်သည်
맞아요. 계단이 어두우면 휴대폰 불을 켜세요.
Right. If the stairs are dark, turn on your phone's light.
majayo gedani eodu-umyeon hyudaepon bureul kyeoseyo
sm: "-(으)면" means "if…" and is added to the end of the condition.
"-(으)면" means "if…" and is added to the end of the condition.

i: Means "if you want to…". Used to tell how to reach a goal. It is like "if you want to…, (in order) to…" in English.
Means "if you want to…". Used to tell how to reach a goal. It is like "if you want to…, (in order) to…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으려면", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-려면"을 붙입니다. 뒤에는 "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요", "-(으)면 돼요"가 옵니다.
After a 받침 add "-으려면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려면". After it comes "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요" or "-(으)면 돼요".
c: 받다 လက်ခံရရှိသည်
လက်ခံရသည်၊ ရသည်
만들다 လုပ်သည်၊ ပြုလုပ်သည်
လုပ်သည်၊ ပြုလုပ်သည်
잘하다 တော်သည်၊ ကျွမ်းကျင်သည်
if you want to be good at
တော်သည်၊ ကျွမ်းကျင်သည်
e: To go to Korea, you have to take a test.
To open a bank account, you need your residence card.
ဘဏ်စာအုပ်၊ ဘဏ်အကောင့်
လုပ်သည်၊ ပြုလုပ်သည်
시청에 가려면 몇 번 버스를 타야 돼요?
sicheonge garyeomyeon myeot beon beoseureul taya dwaeyo?
Which bus do I have to take to go to City Hall?
to ride, to take (a bus, boat)
If you want to be good at Korean, practice every day.
ကောင်းကောင်း လုပ်သည်၊ တော်သည်
tp: 길을 묻거나 절차를 물을 때 가장 쓸모 있는 문형입니다. "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?"
It is the most useful pattern for asking the way or asking about procedures: "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?" (What do I have to do to…?)
pr: 가려면 if you want to go
dl: 체류 기간을 연장하려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?
What do I have to do to extend my period of stay?
သက်တမ်းတိုးသည်
cheryu giganeul yeonjangharyeomyeon eotteoke haeya dwaeyo?
You have to apply at the immigration office.
What do I need to apply?
You need your passport, residence card and certificate of enrollment.
နိုင်ငံကူးလက်မှတ်
sm: "-(으)려면" means "if you want to…", and the way to do it comes after.
"-(으)려면" means "if you want to…", and the way to do it comes after.
qz: "What do I have to do to…?"를 한국어로?

i: Tells the purpose of going or coming. It is like "go/come to + verb" (go to eat) in English.
Tells the purpose of going or coming. It is like "go/come to + verb" (go to eat) in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으러", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-러"를 붙이고, 뒤에 "가다, 오다, 다니다"를 씁니다.
After a 받침 add "-으러"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-러", then use "가다, 오다, 다니다".
c: 공부하다 စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
go out (to have fun), go on a trip
배우다 သင်ယူသည်
e: I came to Korea to study.
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
Come over and visit on the weekend.
စနေ တနင်္ဂနွေ
I'm going to the bank to take out money.
(ငွေ) ထုတ်သည်
tp: In English "go" comes first (go to eat), but in Korean "가요" comes at the end (먹으러 가요).
In English "go" comes first (go to eat), but in Korean "가요" comes at the end (먹으러 가요).
뒤에는 움직이는 동사(가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다)만 옵니다. 다른 동사가 오면 "-(으)려고"를 씁니다.
Only verbs of movement (가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다) can come after it. With other verbs, use "-(으)려고".
가는 곳은 "에"로 말합니다. "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요."
Say the place you go to with "에": "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요." (I'm going to a restaurant to eat.)
dl: ဆမ်၊ ဘယ် သွားမလို့လဲ။
I'm going to the post office to send a package.
저도 편지를 부치러 가야 하는데 같이 가요.
I have to go mail a letter too, so let's go together.
jeodo pyeonjireul buchireo gaya haneunde gachi gayo
sm: "-(으)러 가요/와요" means "go/come to + verb".
"-(으)러 가요/와요" means "go/come to + verb".
qz: "-(으)러" 뒤에 올 수 있는 것은? 가다 / 먹다

i: Tells the purpose of an action. It is like "to…, in order to…" in English.
Tells the purpose of an action. It is like "to…, in order to…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으려고", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-려고"를 붙입니다. 뒤에 어떤 동사나 올 수 있습니다.
After a 받침 add "-으려고"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려고". Any verb can come after it.
c: နေထိုင်သည်
e: I came to open a bank account.
ဘဏ်စာအုပ်၊ ဘဏ်အကောင့်
လုပ်သည်၊ ပြုလုပ်သည်
I'm saving money to send to my family.
I'm learning Korean to study at a Korean university.
စာသင်သည်၊ လေ့လာသည်
I went to bed early so I could get up early.
အိပ်ရာထသည်၊ နိုးသည်
tp: In English you usually say the action first and then the purpose after "to, in order to", but in Korean the purpose comes first and the action comes after.
In English you usually say the action first and then the purpose after "to, in order to", but in Korean the purpose comes first and the action comes after.
뒤에 시키는 말이나 같이 하자는 말은 잘 쓰지 않습니다. 그때는 "-(으)려면"을 씁니다.
Orders and suggestions are not usually used after it. In that case, use "-(으)려면".
창구에서 온 까닭을 말할 때 "~(으)려고 왔어요", "~(으)려고요"라고 합니다.
At a counter, to say why you came, say "~(으)려고 왔어요" or "~(으)려고요".
dl: How can I help you? (Why did you come?)
I came to pay my tuition.
Please give me your bankbook and ID card.
ဘဏ်စာအုပ်၊ ဘဏ်အကောင့်
မှတ်ပုံတင်ကတ်၊ သက်သေခံကတ်
ပေးသည် (주세요 = ... ပေးပါ)
ဒီမှာ၊ ဒီနေရာ
sm: "-(으)려고" means "in order to…", and the purpose is said first.
"-(으)려고" means "in order to…", and the purpose is said first.

i: Used to add the reason for what you just said. It tells something the listener does not know. It feels like "…, you see" or "because…" in English.
Used to add the reason for what you just said. It tells something the listener does not know. It feels like "…, you see" or "because…" in English.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-거든요"를 붙입니다. 지난 일은 "-았/었거든요", 명사는 "(이)거든요"입니다.
Take "-다" off and add "-거든요". For the past, use "-았/었거든요"; for nouns, use "(이)거든요".
c: 바쁘다 အလုပ်များသည်
အလုပ်များသည်
because it's (my) first time, you see
e: I'm leaving early today. I have plans, you see.
ချိန်းဆိုမှု၊ အစီအစဉ်
I won't eat. I ate a little while ago, you see.
I'm not sure. It's my first time here, you see.
ဒီမှာ၊ ဒီနေရာ
I'm a little tired these days. I have a lot of assignments, you see.
ဒီရက်ပိုင်း
ပင်ပန်းသည်
အိမ်စာ၊ တာဝန်
tp: 까닭이 뒤에 옵니다. "-아서/어서"와 순서가 반대입니다. "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."
The reason comes after. The order is the opposite of "-아서/어서": "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."
[거든뇨]로 소리 납니다.
It is pronounced [거든뇨].
dl: 샘 씨, 오늘 동아리 모임에 안 가요?
Sam, aren't you going to the club meeting today?
တွေ့ဆုံပွဲ၊ အစည်းအဝေး
saem ssi, oneul dongari mo-ime an gayo?
네, 못 가요. 몸이 좀 안 좋거든요.
No, I can't go. I'm not feeling well, you see.
ခန္ဓာကိုယ်
(몸이 안 좋다 = to not feel well)
ne, mot gayo momi jom an jokeodeunyo
ဘယ်နေရာ နာလဲ။
ဘယ်အပိုင်း (က)၊ ဘယ်နေရာ (က)
နာသည်၊ ဖျားသည်
I've had a headache since yesterday, you see.
မှ၊ ကတည်းက
နာသည်၊ ဖျားသည်
sm: "-거든요"는 앞말의 까닭을 뒤에서 덧붙입니다.
"-거든요" adds the reason for what was said before, after it.
qz: 격식 있는 자리에서 쓰는 말은? -거든요 / -기 때문입니다

i: 좋은 결과가 생긴 까닭을 고마워하며 말할 때 씁니다. 영어 "thanks to…"입니다.
Used to give the reason for a good result, with thanks. It is like "thanks to…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-은 덕분에", 받침이 없으면 "-ㄴ 덕분에"를 붙입니다. 명사는 "명사 + 덕분에"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-은 덕분에"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ 덕분에". For nouns, use "noun + 덕분에".
c: ပေးသည် (ရိုသေစကား)
교수님 ပါမောက္ခ
e: Thanks to your help, we finished quickly.
Thanks to the professor, I learned Korean well.
I've been well, thanks to you.
Thanks to practicing hard, I passed the test.
tp: 좋은 일에만 씁니다. 나쁜 일에는 "때문에"나 "-는 바람에"를 씁니다.
Use it only for good things. For bad things, use "때문에" or "-는 바람에".
"덕분에 잘 지냈어요", "덕분입니다"는 안부 인사에 대한 대답으로 굳어 있습니다.
"덕분에 잘 지냈어요" and "덕분입니다" are set phrases used to answer "How have you been?"
dl: 샘 씨, 이번 시험에서 백 점을 받았어요. 잘했어요.
Sam, you got 100 points on this exam. Well done.
saem ssi, ibeon siheomeseo baek jeomeul badasseoyo jalhaesseoyo
감사합니다. 진하 씨가 잘 가르쳐 준 덕분입니다.
Thank you. It's thanks to Jinha teaching me well.
ကျေးဇူးတင်သည်
သင်ကြားသည်
to give (-아/어 주다 = do for someone)
gamsahamnida jinha ssiga jal gareucheo jun deokpunimnida
Keep working hard from now on too.
sm: "덕분에"는 좋은 결과의 까닭을 고마워하며 말합니다.
"덕분에" gives the reason for a good result, with thanks.
qz: 좋은 일의 까닭에 쓰는 말은? 때문에 / 덕분에

i: A verb describes a noun. It shows something happening now or done regularly. It is like "the … who/that …" in English.
A verb describes a noun. It shows something happening now or done regularly. It is like "the … who/that …" in English.
m: 동사와 "있다/없다"의 "-다"를 떼고 "-는"을 붙인 뒤 명사를 놓습니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(살다 → 사는).
Take "-다" off verbs and "있다/없다", add "-는", then put the noun. A ㄹ 받침 drops (살다 → 사는).
c: 일하다 အလုပ်လုပ်သည်
အလုပ်လုပ်သည်
살다 နေထိုင်သည်
နေထိုင်သည်
e: What is the work you are doing now?
The person standing over there is the teaching assistant.

At school, the safest speech style is "-습니다/-습니까" with professors and "-아요/어요" with friends. Use casual speech (반말) only when the other person suggests it first.
한국어와 영어의 가장 큰 차이 세 가지: ① 동사가 끝에 온다 ② 조사가 명사 뒤에 붙는다(영어의 전치사는 명사 앞에 온다) ③ "will, want to, must, don't, if"에 해당하는 말이 모두 동사 뒤에 붙는다.

The three biggest differences between Korean and English: ① The verb comes at the end. ② Particles come after nouns (English prepositions come before nouns). ③ The words for "will, want to, must, don't, if" all come after the verb.
